069/**
070 * Utility class for Date/Time handling. Parsing/formatting SQL
071 * Date/Time/TimeStamp to/from text.
072 */
073public class DateTime {
074  private DateTime() {}
075
076  private static final Logger logger = JStuff.getLogger();
077
078  private static final Map<JDBCType, List<DateTimeFormatter>> dateTimeParsersMap
079      = new EnumMap<>(JDBCType.class);
080  private static final Map<JDBCType, DateTimeFormatter> dateTimeFormatterMap
081      = new EnumMap<>(JDBCType.class);
082
083  private static DateTimeFormatter strict(DateTimeFormatter dtf) {
084    return dtf.withResolverStyle(ResolverStyle.STRICT);
085  }
086
087  /** A style is one or more formats. Used to specify date types for parse. */
088  public enum DateParseStyle {
089    /** Custom Month/Day/Year */
090    MDY,
091    /** Some well know ISO formats. */
092    ISO,
093    /** All of the above. */
094    ALL
095  }
096  private static DateParseStyle date_parse = DateParseStyle.ALL;
097
098  private static DateTimeFormatter date_formatter = strict(getMDYFormatter());
099  private static DateTimeFormatter time_formatter = strict(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_TIME);
100  private static DateTimeFormatter timestamp_formatter
101      = strict(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_DATE_TIME);
102
103  static {
104    if (Boolean.FALSE) {
105      date_parse = DateParseStyle.ALL;
106      date_formatter = ISO_LOCAL_DATE;
107      time_formatter = DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_TIME;
108      timestamp_formatter = DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_DATE_TIME;
109    }
110  }
111
112  /**
113   * Check if column is a handled; must be JDBC date/type and text component.
114   * @param comp
115   * @return true is OK
116   */
117  public static boolean isHandledDateTimeComp(RSC comp) {
118    return comp instanceof JTextComponent && dateTimeHandled.contains(comp.getColumnJDBCType());
119  }
120
121  /**
122   * Check if jdbcType is handled; must be JDBC date/type.
123   * @param jdbcType
124   * @return true is OK
125   */
126  public static boolean isHandledDateTimeJDBCType(JDBCType jdbcType) {
127    return dateTimeHandled.contains(jdbcType);
128  }
129
130  /**
131   * Check if the component is a valid date/time. To avoid exceptions, first
132   * use {@link #isHandledDateTimeComp(dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.SSComponentInterface)}.
133   * @param text The text to validate
134   * @param comp The component that the text is derived from
135   * @return
136   */
137  public static boolean dateTimeColumnValidate(String text, RSC comp) {
138    DtoParse dtoParse = internalDateTimeColumnParse(text, comp);
139    return !dtoParse.isError();
140  }
141
142  /**
143   * Get a list of parsers for date/time of the specified JDBCType.
144   * The first parser are typically used in order, the first success wins.
145   *
146   * @param jdbcType
147   * @return list of parser
148   */
149  // TODO: General this to formatter for any jdbcType? maybe part of
150  // per sscomponent lookup.
151  // TODO: API for working with formatter/parsing maps.
152  // TODO: date/time formatters per component with app map as backup/default.
153  public static List<DateTimeFormatter> getDateTimeParsers(JDBCType jdbcType) {
154    return Collections.unmodifiableList(getInternalDateTimeParsers(jdbcType, null));
155  }
156
157  private static final ImmutableMap<SsFormat, List<DateTimeFormatter>> ssFormatters
158      = new ImmutableMap.Builder<SsFormat, List<DateTimeFormatter>>()
159            .put(SsFormat.DATE_MMDDYYYY_SLASH,
160                 List.of(strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("M/d/uuuu")),
161                         strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MMdduuuu"))))
162            .put(SsFormat.DATE_DDMMYYYY_SLASH,
163                 List.of(strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("d/M/uuuu")),
164                         strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("ddMMuuuu"))))
165            .put(SsFormat.TIME_HHMMSS, List.of(strict(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_TIME),
166                                               strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HHmmss"))))
167            .put(SsFormat.TIMESTAMP_YYYYMMDD_STROKE_HHMMSS_SSSZ,
168                 List.of(strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("uuuu-M-d HH:mm:ss[.SSS[ xxx]]"))))
169            .buildOrThrow();
170
171  private static List<DateTimeFormatter> getInternalDateTimeParsers(RSC comp) {
172    return getInternalDateTimeParsers(comp.getColumnJDBCType(), comp.getSsFormat());
173  }
174  private static List<DateTimeFormatter> getInternalDateTimeParsers(JDBCType jdbcType,
175                                                                    SsFormat ssFormat) {
176    if (ssFormat != null) {
177      List<DateTimeFormatter> rv = ssFormatters.get(ssFormat);
178      if (rv != null)
179        return rv;
180    }
181    return dateTimeParsersMap.computeIfAbsent(jdbcType, (type) -> {
182      return switch (type) {
183        case DATE ->
184          new ArrayList<>(switch (date_parse) {
185            case MDY -> List.of(getMDYParser());
186            case ISO ->
187              List.of(strict(DateTimeFormatter.BASIC_ISO_DATE),
188                      strict(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_DATE));
189            case ALL ->
190              List.of(getMDYParser(), strict(DateTimeFormatter.BASIC_ISO_DATE),
191                      strict(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_DATE));
192            default -> null;
193          });
194        case TIME -> new ArrayList<>(List.of(strict(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_TIME)));
195        case TIMESTAMP -> {
196          ArrayList<DateTimeFormatter> l;
197          l = new ArrayList<>(getLongTimestampParsers());
198          l.addAll(List.of(strict(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_DATE_TIME),
199                           //strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("uuuu-M-d HH:mm:ss"),
200                           strict(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_DATE)));
201          yield l;
202        }
203        default -> null;
204      };
205    });
206  }
207
208  /**
209   * Get formatter to produce date/time text for the specified JDBCType.
210   *
211   * @param jdbcType
212   * @return text formatter
213   */
214  public static DateTimeFormatter getDateTimeFormatter(JDBCType jdbcType) {
215    return dateTimeFormatterMap.computeIfAbsent(jdbcType, (type) -> {
216      return switch (type) {
217        case DATE -> date_formatter;
218        case TIME -> time_formatter;
219        case TIMESTAMP -> timestamp_formatter;
220        default -> null;
221      };
222    });
223  }
224
225  private static DateTimeFormatter getMDYFormatter() {
226    return strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MM/dd/uuuu"));
227  }
228
229  private static DateTimeFormatter getMDYParser() {
230    return strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("M/d/uuuu"));
231  }
232
233  // These patterns have optional fraction and TZ.
234  // The one with '-' is like ISO, but no 'T'.
235  private static List<DateTimeFormatter> getLongTimestampParsers() {
236    return List.of(strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("M/d/uuuu HH:mm:ss[.SSS [xxx]]")),
237                   strict(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("uuuu-M-d HH:mm:ss[.SSS[ xxx]]")));
238  }
239
240  private record DtoParse(Temporal dto, boolean isError, Exception ex) {}
241
242  private static final Set<JDBCType> dateTimeHandled
243      = EnumSet.of(JDBCType.DATE, JDBCType.TIME, JDBCType.TIMESTAMP);
244
245  private static DtoParse internalDateTimeColumnParse(String text, RSC comp) {
246    List<DateTimeFormatter> formatters = getInternalDateTimeParsers(comp);
247    if (formatters == null || formatters.isEmpty())
248      throw new IllegalArgumentException("only JTextComponent handled");
249    if (text.isBlank())
250      return new DtoParse(null, !comp.getAllowNull(), null); // maybe error
251
252    Exception tex = null;
253    for (DateTimeFormatter formatter : formatters) {
254      try {
255        Temporal dto = null;
256        switch (comp.getColumnJDBCType()) {
257          case TIME -> dto = LocalTime.parse(text, formatter);
258          case DATE -> dto = LocalDate.parse(text, formatter);
259          case TIMESTAMP -> {
260            // Prefer date/time but handle date only.
261            TemporalAccessor dt = formatter.parseBest(text, OffsetDateTime::from,
262                                                      LocalDateTime::from, LocalDate::from);
263            dto = switch (dt) {
264              case LocalDateTime ldt -> ldt;
265              case LocalDate ld -> LocalDateTime.of(ld, LocalTime.of(0, 0));
266              default -> null; // impossible
267            };
268          }
269        }
270        return new DtoParse(dto, false, null);
271      } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
272        logger.log(
273            DEBUG,
274            () -> sf("%s at '%s', %s' fails for '%s' index %d", comp.getColumnForLog(),
275                     text.substring(ex.getErrorIndex()), formatter, text, ex.getErrorIndex()));
276        tex = ex;
277      }
278    }
279    return new DtoParse(null, true, tex);
280  }
281
282  /**
283   * Parse the specified text using this column's type's default parser,
284   * and return the corresponding {@link java.time} object; for example,
285   * {@link java.time.LocalDate}.
286   * @param text new text
287   * @param comp target column
288   * @return a date/time object, null if can't parse
289   */
290  public static Temporal getDateTimeObject(String text, RSC comp) {
291    DtoParse dtoParse = internalDateTimeColumnParse(text, comp);
292    return dtoParse.dto();
293  }
294
295  /**
296   * Parse the specified text using this column's type's default parser,
297   * and return the corresponding {@link java.time} object; for example,
298   * {@link java.time.LocalDate}.
299   * @param text new text
300   * @param comp target column
301   * @return a date/time object, null if can't parse
302   */
303  public static Object getSQLDateTimeObject(String text, RSC comp) {
304    DtoParse dtoParse = internalDateTimeColumnParse(text, comp);
305    if (dtoParse.isError())
306      return null;
307    JDBCType jdbcType = comp.getColumnJDBCType();
308    Temporal dto = dtoParse.dto();
309    return switch (jdbcType) {
310      case DATE -> Date.valueOf((LocalDate) dto);
311      case TIME -> Time.valueOf((LocalTime) dto);
312      case TIMESTAMP -> Timestamp.valueOf((LocalDateTime) dto);
313      default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException(sf("%s not handled", jdbcType));
314    };
315  }
316
317  /**
318   * Using the formatter for the column's specifiedJDBCType,
319   * format the column's specified value.
320   * Return empty string if column is null.
321   * @param comp target column
322   * @return text for column
323   * @throws java.sql.SQLException
324   */
325  public static String getDateTimeText(RSC comp) throws SQLException {
326    JDBCType jdbcType = comp.getColumnJDBCType();
327    // TODO: should there be a way to do a switch on type, use getDate...?
328    Object o = comp.getRowSet().getObject(comp.getColumnIndex());
329    // TODO: derived 3rd arg from comp.getSsFormat
330    return getDateTimeText(o, jdbcType, null);
331  }

333  /**
334   * Using the formatter for the column's specifiedJDBCType,
335   * format the column's specified value.
336   * Return empty string if column is null.
337   * @param jdbcDateTimeObject convert this to text
338   * @param comp target column
339   * @return text for column
340   */
341  public static String getDateTimeText(Object jdbcDateTimeObject, RSC comp) {
342    JDBCType jdbcType = comp.getColumnJDBCType();
343    // TODO: derived 3rd arg from comp.getSsFormat
344    return getDateTimeText(jdbcDateTimeObject, jdbcType, null);
345  }
346
347  /**
348   * Using the formatter for the column's specifiedJDBCType,
349   * format the column's specified value.
350   * Return empty string if column is null.
351   * <p>
352   * The corresponding java.sql and java.time objects are handled the same;
353   * for example, Date and LocalDate.
354   *
355   * @param jdbcDateTimeObject convert this to text
356   * @param jdbcTypefix
357   * @return date/time text for column
358   * @throws SQLException if database access error
359   */
360  private static String getDateTimeText(Object jdbcDateTimeObject, JDBCType jdbcType,
361                                        DateTimeFormatter _formatter) {
362    if (jdbcDateTimeObject instanceof String s)
363      return s;
364    if (jdbcDateTimeObject == null)
365      return "";
366    DateTimeFormatter formatter = _formatter != null ? _formatter : getDateTimeFormatter(jdbcType);
367    if (formatter == null)
368      throw new IllegalArgumentException(sf("%s not handled", jdbcType));
369
370    switch (jdbcType) {
371      case TIME -> {
372        LocalTime lt = jdbcDateTimeObject instanceof LocalTime lt1
373                           ? lt1
374                           : ((Time) jdbcDateTimeObject).toLocalTime();
375        return lt.format(formatter);
376      }
377      case DATE -> {
378        LocalDate ld = jdbcDateTimeObject instanceof LocalDate ld1
379                           ? ld1
380                           : ((Date) jdbcDateTimeObject).toLocalDate();
381        return ld.format(formatter);
382      }
383      case TIMESTAMP -> {
384        LocalDateTime ldt = jdbcDateTimeObject instanceof LocalDateTime ldt1
385                                ? ldt1
386                                : ((Timestamp) jdbcDateTimeObject).toLocalDateTime();
387        return ldt.format(formatter);
388      }
389      default -> {
390        // Impossible since have a formatter.
391        throw new IllegalArgumentException(sf("Impossible: %s", jdbcType));
392      }
393    }
394  }
395
396  // These unused static methods, could be revived and take a JDBCType param.
397  // That's basically what getDateTimeText(...) does for formatting
398  // and getSQLDateTimeObject(...) for parsing.
399  // See getDateTimeObject(...) for returning java.time object.
400
401  static {
402    if (Boolean.FALSE) {
403      getSQLDate("");
404      getStringDate(null);
405    }
406  }
407
408  /**
409   * Convert string to Date using default parser.
410   *
411   * @param _strDate date string in "[m]m/[d]d/yyyy" format
412   *
413   * @return return SQL date for the string specified
414   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if data conversion fails
415   */
416  // TODO: check that all callers handle excepted as needed
417  private static Date getSQLDate(String _strDate) throws IllegalArgumentException {
418    if (_strDate == null) {
419      return null;
420    }
421    String strDate = _strDate.trim();
422    if (strDate.isEmpty()) {
423      return null;
424    }
425
426    List<DateTimeFormatter> formatters = getInternalDateTimeParsers(JDBCType.DATE, null);
427    if (formatters == null || formatters.isEmpty())
428      return null;
429
430    for (DateTimeFormatter formatter : formatters) {
431      try {
432        return Date.valueOf(LocalDate.parse(_strDate, formatter));
433      } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
434        logger.log(
435            DEBUG,
436            () -> sf("'%s' fails for '%s' index %d", formatter, _strDate, ex.getErrorIndex()));
437      }
438    }
439    return null;
440  }
441
442  /**
443   * Format Date using default formatter.
444   * @param _date
445   * @return
446   */
447  private static String getStringDate(Date _date) {
448    DateTimeFormatter formatter = getDateTimeFormatter(JDBCType.DATE);
449    return _date.toLocalDate().format(formatter);
450  }
